1␟compulsory \"apprenticeship\" to their: A transition system in the British Caribbean after 1834 that kept the formerly enslaved legally bound to work for their old masters for years before any real freedom — emancipation on paper, forced labor in practice.
3␟letting courts bind Black children: Postwar Southern laws that let courts forcibly assign Black children as unpaid "apprentices" to white guardians — often the family's former enslaver — until adulthood, frequently over the parents' objections. Slavery rebranded.
9␟Peace Policy: President Grant's approach to Native nations, pitched as assimilation instead of extermination. In practice the army kept breaking treaties to clear land for railroads and settlers, and the violence continued anyway.
10␟a joint committee of Congress took th: An 1871 congressional investigation that gathered thousands of pages of testimony and published a thirteen-volume report documenting Ku Klux Klan terror and violence across the South.
13␟the rifle clubs: Armed white paramilitary bands in the post-Civil War South that broke up Republican meetings by force, intimidated Black voters with displays of weapons, and murdered Black leaders to overturn elections.
14␟paraded with cannon to intimidate Bla: An 1875 episode in Clinton, Mississippi, where armed white "rifle clubs" attacked a Republican gathering and went on to kill dozens of Black residents — part of a campaign of terror to seize the state by force.
